value.zh: 这一关的问题是：相机拍下的这张小图，存进计算机是什么样子？照着画面把每个像素的数填进格子；格子摆成什么形状，图就存成什么形状。
value.en: This level asks: what does this small picture from the camera look like once it is stored in the computer? Following the picture, fill in each pixel's number; the shape of the grid is the shape the image is stored in.

value.zh: 检查台判断得了答案，却碰不到图里的一个数。工作台从这里补起：相机把光变成数，计算机存下的就是这些数。这一章的灰度图里，0 是黑，1 是白，中间的数是不同深浅的灰。
value.en: The station could judge answers but could not touch a single number of an image. The workbench starts here: the camera turns light into numbers, and those numbers are what the computer stores. In this chapter's grey images 0 is black, 1 is white and the numbers between are shades of grey.

why: channel's setting names a position (0, 1, 2), not a colour: the same board, renamed

review [8]: 0B1 teaches one object seen under another viewpoint and light, and rejects a reshaped object; name the point by what it is (appearance variation), not intra-class variation (different instances of one class), which slide 28 does not name and the level marks wrong

value.zh: 外观变化（视角与光照）
value.en: appearance variation (viewpoint and illumination)

value.zh: 同一个物体换了视角或光照，拍出的图几乎每个像素都变了，物体本身却没有变；物体自身的形状变了才是另一个物体。讲义列出的无关变化还有大小和距离、背景、遮挡。识别因此不能记住像素，要找对这些无关变化有容忍度的表示。
value.en: Seen from another viewpoint or under another light, one object yields an image in which nearly every pixel has changed while the object has not; only a change in the object's own shape makes it another object. The lecture's other irrelevant changes are size and distance, background and occlusion. Recognition therefore cannot memorise pixels; it needs a representation tolerant of these irrelevant changes.

ops.value: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/01-introduction.md §3 (why recognition is hard, slide 28: size and distance, viewpoint and pose, lighting, background, occlusion)

value.zh: 同一类、甚至同一个物体的照片，会因大小和距离、视角和姿态、光照、背景、遮挡而大不相同：几乎每个像素都变了，物体却没有变。识别因此不能记住像素，要找对这些无关变化有容忍度的表示。
value.en: Photos of one class, even of one object, differ greatly with size and distance, viewpoint and pose, lighting, background and occlusion: nearly every pixel changes while the object does not. Recognition therefore cannot memorise pixels; it needs a representation tolerant of these irrelevant changes.

value.zh: 类内变化
value.en: intra-class variation

why: Second loop, chapter 0: review findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 (honest claims, neutral names, the material decides)

You get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it, and judge each statement about the scene: true in every candidate, it holds; false in every one, it does not; true in some and false in others, it is undetermined.

Here an opaque screen stands in the scene and hides what is behind it: a part lost to <wiki-ref to="occlusion"></wiki-ref> has not one pixel in the image. As before you get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it.

激光测距：到最近的人 3.4 米

why.zh: 这是按单位配的：米配米、像素坐标配像素坐标。身高不是距离，一个点不是一个框，人数也不是类别：参照和预测量的是同一种东西，才检验得了它。
why.en: That pairs by unit: metres with metres, pixel coordinates with pixel coordinates. A height is not a distance, one point is not a box, and a head count is not a class: a reference tests a prediction only when both measure the same thing.

value.en: In <level-ref to="0C1"></level-ref> even what the image shows allowed several explanations. You get the image and several candidate scenes that all render it, and judge each statement about the scene: true in every candidate, it holds; false in every one, it does not; true in some and false in others, it is undetermined.

why: Second loop, chapter 1: review findings 9, 10, 12, 13, 18, 20 (single-knob benches judged on submit, the fov relation on screen, naive answers with reasons, shape without the picture, zoom from the window only)

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点穿过针孔，落在像平面的什么位置？同一个物体离得越远，像怎样变？两个任务各只开一个旋钮：先横向移动一点，再前后移动一支箭。先想好放在哪里再按「检查」，检查之后才画出光线和像；像落到圆圈标出的目标上才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: where on the image plane does a point land after passing the hole, and how does the image change as the object moves away? Each of the two tasks opens one knob: first move a point sideways, then move an arrow in depth. Decide where to put it before you press Check; the rays and the image are drawn only once you check. It is right when the image lands on the circled target.

value.zh: 检查一次 Z = 2，看像有多高；距离加倍，像高会怎样？
value.en: Check once at Z = 2 and see how tall the image is; what happens to it when the depth doubles?

value.zh: 检查一次 f = 1 时的像高，再想 f 要变成几倍。
value.en: Check the image height once at f = 1, then work out how many times longer f must be.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？先想好哪一档光圈行，再按「检查」：检查之后，曲线才画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? Decide which stop will do before you press Check: only then does the curve draw each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

value.zh: 检查过 f/2 之后，比较曲线低于门槛的那一段：光圈收小一档，模糊圈和这一段各会怎样？
value.en: Once f/2 is checked, look at the stretch of the curve below the threshold: one stop smaller, what happens to the blur circles and to that stretch?

value.zh: 每收小一档，进光量就只剩四分之一。
value.en: Each stop smaller leaves a quarter of the light.

value.zh: 上一个任务里读到过视场：焦距变长，它往哪边变？乙要占满 20 mm 的传感器，像要多高？
value.en: The last task read out the field of view: which way does it move as the focal length grows? To fill the 20 mm sensor, how tall must B's image be?

why.zh: 把像素数当成毫米代进了 h/f = H/Z：100 像素不是 100 mm。传感器 20 mm 排 200 个像素，每个像素 0.1 mm，100 像素只有 10 mm；按 500 mm 的焦距，像会有 100 mm 高，比整块传感器还高。
why.en: That puts the pixel count into h/f = H/Z as millimetres, but 100 pixels are not 100 mm. The sensor holds 200 pixels in 20 mm, so a pixel is 0.1 mm and 100 pixels are 10 mm; at f = 500 mm the image would be 100 mm tall, taller than the whole sensor.

value.zh: 上一个任务的台子在 f = 50 mm 时读出了以像素计的焦距和视场。
value.en: At f = 50 mm the bench in the last task read out the focal length in pixels and the field of view.

value.zh: 从针孔看传感器的上边和下边：半个传感器高除以焦距，是半个视场角的正切。
value.en: Seen from the pinhole, half the sensor's height over the focal length is the tangent of half the view angle.

ops.zh: 这一关新在方向：从坐标换到数组。先按下标点出像素；再只凭数组的形状说出图的宽和高，图本身不给；最后把<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>报出的尺寸换成数组形状。每一问都要点中那一格或选对那一对数。
ops.en: What is new is the direction: from coordinates to arrays. Pick a pixel by its index; then say an image's width and height from its array shape alone, with no image to count; last, turn a size reported by <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref> into an array shape. Each task wants the right cell or the right pair of numbers.

why.zh: 把 I[1, 2] 当成了坐标 (x, y) = (1, 2)：这张图只有第 0、1 两行，y = 2 出了界。数组的第一个下标是行，也就是 y。
why.en: That reads I[1, 2] as the coordinates (x, y) = (1, 2): this image has only rows 0 and 1, so y = 2 is outside it. The array's first index is the row, that is y.

brief.zh: 只给出数组的形状：选出这张图的宽和高。
brief.en: Only the array shape is given: choose the image's width and height.

hint.zh: 形状的每一维数的是什么：行，还是列？
hint.en: What does each entry of the shape count: rows, or columns?

prompt.zh: 一张灰度图，数组形状是 (2, 3)。
prompt.en: A grey image whose array shape is (2, 3).

prompt.zh: 一张灰度图，数组形状是 (480, 640)。
prompt.en: A grey image whose array shape is (480, 640).

why.zh: 把形状当成了 (宽, 高)：形状先数行，(2, 3) 是 2 行、每行 3 个像素，也就是高 2、宽 3。
why.en: That reads the shape as (width, height). A shape counts the rows first: (2, 3) is 2 rows of 3 pixels, so 2 tall and 3 wide.

brief.zh: 由 OpenCV 报出的尺寸，选出图的数组形状。
brief.en: From the size OpenCV reports, choose the image's array shape.

hint.zh: 第一轮里那张已知宽高的照片，OpenCV 先报的是哪一个数？
hint.en: For the photo in the first round whose width and height are known, which number does OpenCV report first?

prompt.zh: 一张宽 640、高 480 的照片，OpenCV 报出的尺寸是 (640, 480)。另一张灰度图，OpenCV 报出 (300, 200)：它的数组形状是？
prompt.en: For a photo 640 wide and 480 tall, OpenCV reports the size (640, 480). For another grey image it reports (300, 200): what is that image's array shape?

prompt.zh: 用 OpenCV 把一张灰度图缩放到尺寸 (64, 32)：得到的数组形状是？
prompt.en: OpenCV resizes a grey image to the size (64, 32): what is the resulting array's shape?

why.zh: 把 OpenCV 的尺寸原样抄成了形状：OpenCV 的尺寸先写宽，是 (宽, 高)；数组形状先写行数，是 (高, 宽)，两者正好反过来。
why.en: That copies OpenCV's size straight into the shape. OpenCV's size puts the width first, (width, height); an array shape puts the rows first, (height, width): the one is the other reversed.

why.zh: 这是把新像素当成旧像素重新编号：原图这一行只有 x = 0 和 x = 1 两个像素，x = 2 落在原图外面。新旧两排一样长，三个新像素中心要分布在两个旧像素占的那段长度上。
why.en: That renumbers the new pixels as if they were old ones: the original row has pixels at x = 0 and x = 1 only, so x = 2 lies outside it. The two rows are equally long, so the three new centres spread over the length the two old pixels cover.

value.zh: 输入一张图和倍数 k：交出同样大小的图，内容是原图中心那个宽、高各为 1/k 的窗口放大 k 倍，只用窗口里的像素。
value.en: Given an image and a factor k, give an image of the same size showing the window at the original's centre, 1/k as wide and as tall, magnified k times, made from the pixels inside that window only.

value.zh: 变焦后的画面只用得到原图的哪些像素？先把它们取出来。
value.en: Which pixels of the original can the zoomed picture use? Take those out first.

value.zh: 窗口宽是原宽的 1/k，左右两边各留下多少？
value.en: The window is 1/k of the width: how much is left over on each side?

value.zh: 放大以后，原来的坐标也跟着放大了。
value.en: After enlarging, the old coordinates are enlarged too.

value.zh: 输入一张图和倍数 k：交出同样大小的图，内容是原图中心放大 k 倍。
value.en: Given an image and a factor k, give an image of the same size showing the original's centre magnified k times.

brief.zh: OpenCV 说这张图的尺寸是 (4, 5)：写出它的数组形状。
brief.en: OpenCV gives this image's size as (4, 5): write its array shape.

hint.zh: 数组的形状先写哪一维？OpenCV 的尺寸先写哪一维？
hint.en: Which dimension does an array shape list first? Which does an OpenCV size list first?

brief.zh: 这张图的数组形状是 (2, 3)：写出它的宽和高。
brief.en: This image's array shape is (2, 3): write its width and height.

value.zh: 这一关新在方向：从坐标换到数组。先按下标点出像素，再从数组的形状读出图的宽和高，最后把<wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>给出的尺寸写成数组形状；OpenCV 把尺寸写成 (宽, 高)。每一问都要点中那一格或写对那两个数。
value.en: What is new is the direction: from coordinates to arrays. Pick a pixel by its index, read an image's width and height off its array shape, then write as an array shape a size given by <wiki-ref to="opencv"></wiki-ref>, which writes sizes as (width, height). Each task wants the right cell or the right two numbers.

value.zh: 台上读得出视场：焦距变了，它往哪边变？
value.en: The bench reads out the field of view: which way does it move as the focal length changes?

value.zh: 比较两档光圈下，曲线低于门槛的那一段有多宽。
value.en: Compare how wide the stretch of the curve below the threshold is at two apertures.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？曲线画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
value.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? The curve draws each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

value.zh: 先看箭在 Z = 2 和 Z = 4 时，像各有多高。
value.en: First see how tall the image is with the arrow at Z = 2 and at Z = 4.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点穿过针孔，落在像平面的什么位置？同一个物体离得越远，像怎样变？两个任务各只开一个旋钮：先横向移动一点，再前后移动一支箭。像落到圆圈标出的目标上才算对。
value.en: This level asks: where on the image plane does a point land after passing the hole, and how does the image change as the object moves away? Each of the two tasks opens one knob: first move a point sideways, then move an arrow in depth. It is right when the image lands on the circled target.

why: Copy step, second loop: review findings 6, 11, 14, 15, 17, 19 (maps read without a picture, the judge's rule stated, no forward reference to (x, y), BGR left to the channels, clipping left to the screen, the crop spec without its method); channel's setting named by position; 1B5's light given a reference; 1B7's arrows no longer called a row

ops.zh: 检测框只把物体圈在一个矩形里，说不出框里哪些像素属于物体。有的输出给每个像素一个数，是一张和照片一样大的图：0 是背景。这一关不给照片，只给这些图；其余的数是什么意思，只能从它们在图上怎样分布读出来。
ops.en: A detection box only rings an object with a rectangle and cannot say which pixels inside it belong to the object. Some outputs give every pixel a number, a map as large as the photo: 0 is background. This level shows no photo, only the maps, so what the other numbers mean has to be read from how they spread across each map.

ops.zh: 这一关新在两处：一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出够用的都算对；三张图的格子里都是数，含义却不同，而画面不给出，含义只能从图上的数本身判断。这一关的问题是：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？类别图里的数能当距离用吗？
ops.en: Two things are new here: a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing those that suffice is right; and the three maps all hold numbers that mean different things, with no picture shown, so the meaning must come from the numbers themselves. This level asks: which output answers 'how far away is that car'? Can the numbers in a class map serve as distances?

value.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数，有的是编号，有的是类别，有的是长度。比较每张图里各片区域的数。
value.en: All three maps hold numbers: some are ids, some classes, some lengths. Compare the numbers of the regions within each map.

value.zh: 两个同类物体在一张图里各有自己的数，还是共用一个？哪张图的数从上往下一路变小，像越来越近的地面？
value.en: Do two objects of one class get a number each in a map, or share one? In which map do the numbers fall steadily from top to bottom, like ground coming nearer?

ops.zh: 只把第二行正中间那个像素的蓝色调到 1，得到 (1, 1, 1)，那是白色：纯蓝还要红和绿都是 0。
ops.en: Raising only the blue number of the middle pixel in the second row gives (1, 1, 1), which is white: pure blue also needs its red and green at 0.

ops.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。这一关反过来问：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？焦距固定为 f = 2。每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出至少两组：选中的每一组像高都是 1，各组的距离互不相同。
ops.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. This level asks the other way: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? The focal length is fixed at f = 2. Each round lists several (height, depth) pairs; choose at least two, every one of them imaging 1 tall and no two at the same depth.

ops.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。要把一个像素的三个数拆开、重新排，工作台还没有这样的元件。新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出每个像素某一个位置上的数，组成一张灰度图，位置在元件上设成 0、1 或 2，就是第一、第二或第三个数；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图依次当作 R、G、B，合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
ops.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and putting them back in another order needs parts the workbench lacks. The new part <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes the number at one position of every pixel as a grey image, the position set on the part to 0, 1 or 2 for the first, second or third number; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> takes three grey images as R, G and B, in that order, and makes them one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

ops.zh: 输入是用 OpenCV 读进来的照片：交出同一张照片，让它在这里显示出本来的颜色。
ops.en: The input is a photo read with OpenCV: give the same photo so that it shows here in its true colours.

ops.zh: 把三个位置的数分别取出来看：天空在哪一张里最亮？蓝天本该亮在哪一种颜色上？
ops.en: Take the numbers at the three positions out one by one: in which of them is the sky brightest? Which colour should a blue sky be bright in?

ops.zh: OpenCV 读进来的照片
ops.en: Photo read with OpenCV

ops.zh: 颜色正确的照片
ops.en: Photo in true colours

ops.zh: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref>弄清了三个数的顺序，还没问它们的大小。电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外，比如 −0.2 或 1.2；这样的值画到屏幕上是什么样子，还没有看过。文件里的像素又常存成<wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>：0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
ops.en: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref> settled the order of the three numbers but not their size. A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1], such as −0.2 or 1.2, and how such values look on a screen has not come up yet. And files often store pixels as <wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>: whole numbers from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

ops.zh: 测试图里画着一个正方形的东西：交出的 S×S 图里，它还得是正方形。结果里每个像素都来自照片，不留空边；它的中心对准照片的中心，对不准时偏左上半个像素。横幅和竖幅的照片都要成立。
ops.en: The test images hold something square, and in the S×S result it must still be square. Every pixel of the result comes from the photo, with no empty borders, and it is centred on the photo's centre, half a pixel towards the top-left where it cannot be exact. It must work for landscape and portrait photos alike.

ops.zh: 输入一张照片和边长 S：交出 S×S 的图，照片里的正方形在图里仍是正方形，画面居中。
ops.en: Given a photo and a side S, give an S×S image, centred on the photo, in which squares stay square.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？先想好哪一档光圈行，再按「检查」：检查之后，曲线才画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。进光量以 3 mm 光圈的进光为 1。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
ops.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? Decide which stop will do before you press Check: only then does the curve draw each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. Light is measured against a 3 mm aperture, which lets in 1. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

ops.zh: 这一关的问题是：要把几个物体全拍进画面，焦距该变长还是变短？三支箭都在 2000 mm 外，台上只有焦距 f 能动。第一个任务要三支都在画面里，中间那支乙又不能太小；第二个任务只拍乙，要它占满画面的高度。
ops.en: This level asks: to get several objects into the frame at once, should the focal length grow or shrink? Three arrows stand 2000 mm away, and only the focal length f turns. The first task wants all three in view without the middle arrow B shrinking too far; the second shows B alone and wants it to fill the frame's height.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：要把一排物体全拍进画面，焦距该变长还是变短？三支箭都在 2000 mm 外，台上只有焦距 f 能动。第一个任务要三支都在画面里，中间那支乙又不能太小；第二个任务只拍乙，要它占满画面的高度。
value.en: This level asks: to get a whole row of objects into the frame, should the focal length grow or shrink? Three arrows stand 2000 mm away, and only the focal length f turns. The first task wants all three in view without the middle arrow B shrinking too far; the second shows B alone and wants it to fill the frame's height.

value.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处两个物体，怎样在一张照片里都清晰？先想好哪一档光圈行，再按「检查」：检查之后，曲线才画出每个深度的模糊圈和清晰的门槛。两个标记都清晰、进光量又不低于 1，才算对。
value.en: This level asks: how can a near and a far object both be sharp in one photo? Decide which stop will do before you press Check: only then does the curve draw each depth's blur circle against the sharpness threshold. It is right when both markers are sharp and the light is at least 1.

value.zh: 输入一张图和边长 S：按同一个比例缩放到短边等于 S，再从中间裁出 S×S。
value.en: Given an image and a side S, scale it by one factor until its short side is S, then crop S×S from the middle.

value.zh: 测试图里画着一个正方形的东西：交出的 S×S 图里，它还得是正方形。多出来的部分从两边平均去掉，除不尽时左上少去掉一个像素。横幅和竖幅的照片都要成立。
value.en: The test images hold something square, and in the S×S result it must still be square. The excess is removed evenly from both sides, one pixel less at the top-left when it does not divide. It must work for landscape and portrait photos alike.

value.zh: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref>弄清了三个数的顺序，还没问它们的大小。电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外，屏幕却只显示得出 0 到 1，超出的部分画成最黑或最白。文件里的像素又常存成<wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>：0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
value.en: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref> settled the order of the three numbers but not their size. A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1], while a screen shows only 0 to 1 and draws whatever lies beyond as the darkest or the brightest. And files often store pixels as <wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>: whole numbers from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

value.zh: 照片（RGB）
value.en: Photo (RGB)

value.zh: 照片（BGR）
value.en: Photo (BGR)

value.zh: 把三个通道分别取出来看：设成 R 取出的那一张，装的是天空的什么颜色？
value.en: Take the three channels out one by one: the one set to R, which colour of the sky does it hold?

value.zh: 输入是按 BGR 存的照片：交出同一张照片按 RGB 存的样子。
value.en: The input is a photo stored as BGR: give the same photo stored as RGB.

value.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。要把一个像素的三个数拆开、重新排，工作台还没有这样的元件。新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出彩色图的一个通道，设成 R、G 或 B，就是每格的第一、第二或第三个数；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
value.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and putting them back in another order needs parts the workbench lacks. The new part <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes one channel out of a colour image, set to R, G or B, the first, second or third number of each cell; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> makes three grey images one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

value.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。这一关反过来问：看到像有多高，能定出物体有多远吗？焦距固定为 f = 2。每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出像高都是 1、距离又各不相同的那几组，全部选对、一组不多才算对。
value.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. This level asks the other way: does the height of an image tell how far away the object is? The focal length is fixed at f = 2. Each round lists several (height, depth) pairs; choose those that all image 1 tall at different depths, all of them and no others.

value.zh: 只把 (1, 1) 的蓝色调到 1，得到 (1, 1, 1)，那是白色：纯蓝还要红和绿都是 0。
value.en: Raising only the blue number of (1, 1) gives (1, 1, 1), which is white: pure blue also needs its red and green at 0.

value.zh: 三张图的格子里都是数：对照图里的物体，判断每张图的数是编号、类别还是长度。
value.en: All three maps hold numbers: compare them with the objects in the picture and decide whether each map's numbers are ids, classes or lengths.

value.zh: 这一关新在两处：一个请求可以有几份够用的输出，选出够用的都算对；三张图的格子里都是数，含义却不同，要对照画面读出来。这一关的问题是：「那辆车离我多远」该由哪一份回答？类别图里的数能当距离用吗？
value.en: Two things are new here: a request may have several sufficient outputs, and choosing those that suffice is right; and the three maps all hold numbers that mean different things, to be read against the picture. This level asks: which output answers 'how far away is that car'? Can the numbers in a class map serve as distances?

value.zh: 检测框只把物体圈在一个矩形里，说不出框里哪些像素属于物体。有的输出给每个像素一个数，是一张和照片一样大的图：0 是背景，其余的数是什么意思，要对照画面读出来。
value.en: A detection box only rings an object with a rectangle and cannot say which pixels inside it belong to the object. Some outputs give every pixel a number, a map as large as the photo: 0 is background, and what the other numbers mean has to be read against the picture.

why: Copy step, second loop: 1C1's intro within length, its brief the task only

ops.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。把一个像素的三个数拆开、重排，要用新元件：<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出每个像素第 0、1 或 2 个位置上的数（在元件上设定），组成一张灰度图；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图依次当作 R、G、B，合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
ops.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and reordering them needs new parts: <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes the number at position 0, 1 or 2 of every pixel, as set on the part, as a grey image; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> takes three grey images as R, G and B, in that order, and makes one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

ops.zh: 输入是用 OpenCV 读进来的照片：交出同一张照片，颜色和本来的一样。
ops.en: The input is a photo read with OpenCV: give the same photo in its true colours.

value.zh: 输入是用 OpenCV 读进来的照片：交出同一张照片，让它在这里显示出本来的颜色。
value.en: The input is a photo read with OpenCV: give the same photo so that it shows here in its true colours.

value.zh: 这一关要接一块电路：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。要把一个像素的三个数拆开、重新排，工作台还没有这样的元件。新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出每个像素某一个位置上的数，组成一张灰度图，位置在元件上设成 0、1 或 2，就是第一、第二或第三个数；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图依次当作 R、G、B，合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
value.en: This level wires a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Taking a pixel's three numbers apart and putting them back in another order needs parts the workbench lacks. The new part <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes the number at one position of every pixel as a grey image, the position set on the part to 0, 1 or 2 for the first, second or third number; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> takes three grey images as R, G and B, in that order, and makes them one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

why: A demonstration course: three ladders to the cores of lectures 1–2, and one optional technical topic

learner.zh: 学过编程和中学数学、没有学过计算机视觉的学习者（COMP90086 的学生）
learner.en: Learners who can program and know school mathematics but have not studied computer vision (COMP90086 students)

endpoint.zh: 看懂一张图从哪里来、能说明什么：针孔投影为什么让一张图定不了深度，透镜为什么在亮和清晰之间取舍，缩放时新像素的值怎样从四个邻居算出。
endpoint.en: Understand where an image comes from and what it can tell: why pinhole projection leaves depth unsettled, why a lens trades light against sharpness, and how resizing works a new pixel out of four neighbours.

scope.zh: 示范课程，覆盖第 1、2 讲的三个核心：反问题（由中心投影、近大远小、尺度歧义逐级搭起）、景深（由对焦、模糊圈搭起）、双线性插值（由采样网格、最近邻、线性插值搭起）。一听就懂的点（图形学与视觉的方向相反、容许模糊圈）只在文案和词条里提到。技术内容（通道顺序）放在主线走完后的可选专题。视觉任务的分类、量化、裁剪等点暂不做成关。
scope.en: A demonstration course covering the three cores of lectures 1–2: the inverse problem (built up from central projection, perspective scaling and scale ambiguity), depth of field (from focus and the blur circle) and bilinear interpolation (from the sampling grid, nearest neighbour and linear interpolation). Points plain from a sentence (graphics and vision run opposite ways, the acceptable blur) are only mentioned in copy and entries. Technical content (channel order) is an optional topic once the main path ends. Vision task types, quantisation and cropping are not levels yet.

where.zh: 投影和光学两个系列：针孔相机台和薄透镜台
where.en: The projection and optics series: the pinhole and thin-lens benches

why.zh: 投影和景深是连续量之间的关系；台子让玩家先预测、再检查，检查后才画出光线和模糊曲线，猜不出来，要按关系算。
why.en: Projection and depth of field are relations between continuous quantities; the bench has the player predict, then check, drawing the rays and the blur curve only after, so the relation must be worked out, not slid into.

where.zh: 尺度歧义和反问题：选择判定（project、claims）
where.en: Scale ambiguity and the inverse problem: choice judges (project, claims)

why.zh: 这两点要练的是判断：哪些物体成一样的像，一张图能确定哪些论断。对错由领域按场景算出，答错时画出两个意见相反、却渲出同一张图的场景。
why.en: What these practise is judgement: which objects image alike, which claims one image settles. The domain computes right and wrong from the scenes and, on a wrong answer, draws two scenes that disagree yet render the same image.

where.zh: 重采样系列每关的第一个任务：在格子上手算采样位置和插值结果
where.en: The first task of each resampling level: working out sample positions and interpolated values on the grid

why.zh: 先亲手当一回机器，算出新像素落在哪里、值是多少，电路才有前因。
why.en: Acting as the machine first, working out where new pixels fall and what they are worth, gives the circuit its reason.

where.zh: 重采样系列和通道顺序专题：图像电路
where.en: The resampling series and the channel-order topic: image circuits

why.zh: 缩放是对每个像素做同一件事，电路把手算的一步变成对整张图的计算，搭出的采样网格成为后面几关的元件。
why.en: Resizing does one thing to every pixel; the circuit turns the hand step into a computation over a whole image, and the sampling grid built becomes a part of the levels after.

about.zh: 回答判断题：选出成一样的像的物体，给关于场景的论断定真假（choice 任务）
about.en: Answer judgement questions: choose objects that image alike, judge claims about a scene (choice tasks)

about.zh: 受控的三维小场景：渲出图像；场景同时是判定用的事实
about.en: A controlled small 3D scene: renders an image; the scene is also the facts the judges use

about.zh: 相机台：针孔相机和薄透镜的参数台
about.en: The camera bench: parameter benches for the pinhole camera and the thin lens

about.zh: 读写像素格：看图的数和画面，填格子（grid 任务）
about.en: Read and write pixel grids: see an image's numbers and picture, fill grids (grid tasks)

about.zh: 图像电路：把图和数接成一块板，搭出的板成为元件
about.en: Image circuits: wire images and numbers into a board; a board built becomes a part

lacks.zh: 每个输出像素只由原图里个别位置的值算出：它不能把一个邻域的像素合起来（平滑、找边），也不会学习，这是下一章存在的理由。
lacks.en: Every output pixel is computed from source values at single positions: it cannot combine a neighbourhood of pixels (smoothing, finding edges) and cannot learn, the reason the next chapter exists.

about.zh: 针孔相机里，物点发出的光只有穿过小孔的那一条落到像平面上：像点在物点和小孔连成的直线上，横向位置 u = fX/Z。
about.en: In a pinhole camera only the ray through the hole reaches the image plane: the image of a point lies on the line through the point and the hole, at u = fX/Z.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §1 (pinhole camera model, slide 11)

wall.zh: 物点挪到哪里，它的像落在哪里？
wall.en: Where does a point's image land as the point moves?

misconception.zh: 像就落在和物点同样的横向位置上（u = X）。
misconception.en: The image lands at the point's own lateral position (u = X).

about.zh: 物体的像高 h = fH/Z：和距离成反比，距离加倍，像缩成一半。
about.en: An object's image height is h = fH/Z: inversely proportional to the distance; twice as far, half as tall.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §1 (image formation, slides 9–11)

wall.zh: 物体离得越远，像小多少？
wall.en: How much smaller does an object image as it moves away?

misconception.zh: 距离每多一点，像就少同样多一点（按差来减）。
misconception.en: Each step farther takes the same amount off the image (a difference, not a ratio).

about.zh: 物高和距离同比放大，像一点不变：一张像只定下物高和距离的比值 H/Z。
about.en: Scale an object's size and distance by the same factor and its image does not change: an image fixes only the ratio H/Z.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §1 (projection loses depth, slides 9–11)

wall.zh: 看到一张像，能知道物体多高、多远吗？
wall.en: From an image, can you tell how tall and how far an object is?

misconception.zh: 物高一样，像就一样高。
misconception.en: Equal heights give equal images.

about.zh: 图形学由场景生成图像；视觉反过来，从图像推回场景。
about.en: Graphics makes an image from a scene; vision goes the other way, from an image back to a scene.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/01-introduction.md §2 (vision and graphics, slide 8)

wall.zh: 视觉要做的和画图有什么不同？
wall.en: How is seeing different from drawing?

about.zh: 从图像推回场景时，常有不止一个场景给出同一张图：投影把深度丢掉了。一张图能确定的只是所有相容场景都同意的事；其余要靠另外的线索（已知的物体大小、第二台相机……）。
about.en: Going from an image back to a scene, more than one scene often gives the same image: projection drops depth. An image settles only what every compatible scene agrees on; the rest needs other cues (a known size, a second camera…).

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/01-introduction.md §2 (vision as an inverse problem, slide 8)

wall.zh: 一张图能确定场景里的哪些事，哪些不能？
wall.en: What can one image settle about the scene, and what not?

misconception.zh: 从像的大小就能读出物体的距离和大小。
misconception.en: An image's size tells how far and how big the object is.

about.zh: 透镜把一大片光收拢，可只能把一个距离上的点收成点；别的距离上的点落成一块斑。
about.en: A lens gathers much more light, but brings the points of only one distance to points; points at other distances land as spots.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §2 (why cameras need lenses, slides 12–13)

wall.zh: 透镜能让远处和近处同时清楚吗？
wall.en: Can a lens make near and far sharp at once?

misconception.zh: 对焦在两个物体中间，两个都清楚。
misconception.en: Focusing halfway makes both sharp.

about.zh: 离焦的点在传感器上落成一块圆斑；光圈越大，进光越多，这块斑也越大。
about.en: An out-of-focus point lands on the sensor as a round spot; the wider the aperture, the more light and the bigger the spot.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §2 (aperture and depth of field, slide 16)

wall.zh: 光圈开大有什么代价？
wall.en: What does a wider aperture cost?

misconception.zh: 光圈越大越好：只是更亮。
misconception.en: The wider the better: it is only brighter.

about.zh: 斑小到眼睛（或一个像素）分不出来，就算清楚。
about.en: A spot too small for the eye (or a pixel) to tell from a point counts as sharp.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §2 (aperture and depth of field, slide 16)

wall.zh: 斑多小算清楚？
wall.en: How small a spot is sharp?

about.zh: 对焦距离前后，模糊圈还小于容许模糊圈的那一段距离。光圈越小，斑长得越慢，这一段越长，可进光也越少。
about.en: The range of distances around the focus where the blur circle stays within the acceptable blur. A smaller aperture grows the spot more slowly and lengthens the range, at the cost of light.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §2 (aperture and depth of field, slide 16)

wall.zh: 怎样让近处和远处同时清楚，又够亮？
wall.en: How do near and far stay sharp together, with light enough?

misconception.zh: 对准其中一个、光圈开大就行。
misconception.en: Focus on one of them and open the aperture.

about.zh: 缩放时，新图每个像素的中心按比例落回原图：新旧两排像素占同样长的一段，新像素中心常落在两个旧像素之间。
about.en: When resizing, each new pixel's centre maps back into the original in proportion: both rows span the same length, so new centres often fall between old pixels.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §4 (cropping and resizing are not the same, slide 34)

wall.zh: 放大一张图时，新像素的中心落在原图的哪里？
wall.en: When an image is enlarged, where do the new pixels' centres fall in the original?

misconception.zh: 新像素的下标就是原图的下标。
misconception.en: A new pixel's index is its place in the original.

about.zh: 每个新像素照抄离它最近的旧像素：快、边缘硬，放大后成块。
about.en: Each new pixel copies the nearest old pixel: fast and hard-edged, blocky when enlarged.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §4 (nearest-neighbour interpolation, slide 35)

wall.zh: 落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，最简单的取值办法是什么？
wall.en: What is the simplest value for a new pixel between two old ones?

misconception.zh: 坐标一律向下取整就是最近的那个。
misconception.en: Rounding every coordinate down picks the nearest pixel.

about.zh: 新像素按它到两个邻居的距离加权：离谁近，谁的份量大；正中间就是两者的平均。
about.en: A new pixel weighs its two neighbours by distance: the nearer counts more; halfway is their average.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §4 (bilinear weights, slide 36)

wall.zh: 新像素一定要等于某一个旧像素吗？
wall.en: Must a new pixel equal one of the old ones?

misconception.zh: 新像素只能照抄某一个旧像素。
misconception.en: A new pixel can only copy an old one.

about.zh: 新像素落在四个旧像素之间时，先横着做两次线性插值，再竖着做一次：四个邻居的加权平均，权重 (1−H)(1−V)、H(1−V)、(1−H)V、HV 加起来是 1。比最近邻平滑，会让锐利的边稍微变软。
about.en: A new pixel among four old ones is two linear interpolations across, then one down: a weighted average of the four, the weights (1−H)(1−V), H(1−V), (1−H)V, HV adding to 1. Smoother than nearest neighbour; it softens sharp edges a little.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §4 (bilinear interpolation, slide 36; trade-offs, slide 37)

wall.zh: 新像素落在四个旧像素围成的方格里，值怎么算？
wall.en: How is a new pixel among four old ones worked out?

misconception.zh: 只横着插一次就够了。
misconception.en: Interpolating across once is enough.

about.zh: 彩色像素的三个数按什么顺序存是约定：OpenCV 读进来的是 B、G、R，Matplotlib 显示时当成 R、G、B，不换就红蓝颠倒。
about.en: The order a colour pixel's three numbers are stored in is a convention: OpenCV reads B, G, R, Matplotlib shows R, G, B; without a swap red and blue trade places.

knowledge.source: docs/Unimelb/26S2/CV/02-basics.md §4 (workshop 2: OpenCV and Matplotlib colour order)

wall.zh: 为什么用 OpenCV 读进来的照片，天是橙色的？
wall.en: Why is the sky orange in a photo read with OpenCV?

misconception.zh: 三个数总是 R、G、B。
misconception.en: The three numbers are always R, G, B.

about.zh: 始终给出设定的数
about.en: Always gives the number it is set to

why.zh: 其余元件只变换输入，造不出一个固定的数（0.5、−1）。
why.en: Every other part only transforms its inputs and cannot make a fixed number (0.5, −1).

about.zh: 给定宽和高，给出每格就是自己 x、y 坐标的两张坐标图
about.en: Given a width and a height, gives the two coordinate images whose cells hold their own x and y

why.zh: 新图的每个像素先要有自己的坐标；没有元件能从两个数造出一整张图。
why.en: Every pixel of the new image first needs its own coordinates, and no part makes a whole image from two numbers.

about.zh: 逐元素给出两者之和
about.en: Gives the element-wise sum of the two

why.zh: 基本算术；减法由它和乘以 −1 接出。
why.en: Basic arithmetic; subtraction is wired from it and multiplying by −1.

about.zh: 逐元素给出两者之积
about.en: Gives the element-wise product of the two

why.zh: 按比例换算坐标、按权重加权都要乘法，加法接不出来。
why.en: Scaling coordinates and weighting both need multiplication, which addition cannot wire.

about.zh: 逐元素给出 a 除以 b
about.en: Gives a divided by b, element by element

why.zh: 宽度比例要除以新宽度，乘法接不出一个随输入变的倒数。
why.en: The width ratio divides by the new width; multiplication cannot wire a reciprocal of an input.

about.zh: 给出图的宽和高
about.en: Gives an image's width and height

why.zh: 电路只拿到图本身时，没有别的元件读得出它的尺寸。
why.en: When a circuit is given only the image, no other part can read its size.

about.zh: 给出不大于它的最大整数
about.en: Gives the largest whole number not above it

why.zh: 算术元件只给出连续的数，取像素要整数坐标。
why.en: The arithmetic parts give continuous numbers, and lookup needs whole coordinates.

about.zh: 在图的整数坐标处取值
about.en: Reads an image at whole-number coordinates

why.zh: 其余元件都在同一个位置上算，没有一个能把原图某处的值搬到新图上。
why.en: Every other part computes in place; none carries a value from somewhere in the original to the new image.

about.zh: 给出彩色像素第 c 个位置上的数组成的灰度图
about.en: Gives the grey image of the numbers at position c of each colour pixel

why.zh: 逐元素的算术把一个像素当一个整体，拆不开它的三个数。
why.en: Element-wise arithmetic treats a pixel as one whole and cannot take its three numbers apart.

about.zh: 把三张灰度图合成一张彩色图
about.en: Makes three grey images one colour image

why.zh: 没有别的元件能从灰度图造出一张三通道的图。
why.en: No other part can make a three-channel image out of grey ones.

about.zh: 采样网格：给定原图和新图的宽高，给出新图每个像素在原图里的坐标（两张源坐标图）
about.en: Sampling grid: given the original's and the new width and height, gives each new pixel's coordinates in the original (two source-coordinate images)

why.zh: 投影、光学和重采样三条梯子各自从浅处起步，互不依赖，玩家可以按兴趣先走哪一条。
why.en: The projection, optics and resampling ladders each start from shallow ground and need nothing from each other; the player may climb whichever first.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

why.zh: 从一台理想的针孔相机和一张像素格起步：场景怎样投到像平面上，透镜怎样让图又亮又清晰，像素又怎样被重新采样。
why.en: Starting from an ideal pinhole camera and a grid of pixels: how a scene projects onto the image plane, how a lens makes an image bright and sharp, and how pixels are resampled.

title.en: An image does not settle depth

task.zh: 在针孔相机台上横向、再前后移动一点，让它的像落进像平面上的圆圈。
task.en: On the pinhole bench, move a point sideways, then in depth, so its image lands in the circle on the image plane.

question.zh: 物点挪到哪里，它的像落在哪里？
question.en: Where does a point's image land as the point moves?

chain.zh: f = 2、Z = 4，目标 u = 1：玩家把点放在 X = 1，检查后像只落到 0.5。
chain.en: With f = 2, Z = 4 and the target at u = 1, the player puts the point at X = 1; checked, the image lands at 0.5 only.

chain.zh: 顺着画出的光线看：像点在点和小孔的连线上，横向位置按 f/Z 缩小，于是放到 X = 2。
chain.en: Following the drawn ray: the image lies on the line through the point and the hole, the sideways position shrunk by f/Z; so X = 2.

chain.zh: 第二个任务只能前后移动：退到两倍远，像只挪到一半处；要到四分之一，得退到四倍远，Z 在分母上。
chain.en: The second task moves only in depth: twice as far, the image moves only halfway in; a quarter needs four times as far, Z is in the denominator.

naive.zh: 像就落在和物点同样的横向位置上（u = X）。
naive.en: The image lands at the point's own lateral position (u = X).

task.zh: 前后移动一支箭、再换像平面距离 f，让像高等于标记。
task.en: Move an arrow in depth, then change the plane distance f, so its image matches the mark.

question.zh: 物体离得越远，像小多少？
question.en: How much smaller does an object image as it moves away?

chain.zh: 箭两端各一条光线穿过小孔，截出的那一段是像：两端各按 f/Z 缩小，像高 h = fH/Z。
chain.en: A ray from each end of the arrow passes the hole; the stretch they cut is the image: each end shrinks by f/Z, so h = fH/Z.

chain.zh: 玩家想每退一步少一截，退到 Z = 3，像高 1.33，没到 1；像高按 1/Z 变，要矮一半就得加倍到 Z = 4。
chain.en: Expecting one unit off per step, the player goes to Z = 3 and gets 1.33, not 1; height goes as 1/Z, so half needs twice as far, Z = 4.

chain.zh: 第二个任务箭不动、只调 f：像高和 f 成正比，三倍高就要三倍 f。
chain.en: In the second the arrow stays and only f turns: height is proportional to f, three times as tall needs three times f.

naive.zh: 距离每多一点，像就少同样多一点（按差来减）。
naive.en: Each step farther takes the same amount off the image (a difference, not a ratio).

task.zh: f = 2，从几组（物高, 距离）里选出像高都是 1、距离各不相同的两组以上。
task.en: With f = 2, choose from several (height, distance) pairs two or more that image 1 tall at different distances.

question.zh: 看到一张像，能知道物体多高、多远吗？
question.en: From an image, can you tell how tall and how far an object is?

chain.zh: 玩家挑了两个一样高的箱子，判定指出距离 2 处高 2 的那个像高是 2。
chain.en: The player picks two crates of one height; the judge points out the one 2 tall at distance 2 images 2 tall.

chain.zh: 按 h = fH/Z 算一遍：高 1 距离 2、高 2 距离 4、高 1.5 距离 3 的像都是 1，H/Z 都是 0.5。
chain.en: Working h = fH/Z: 1 at 2, 2 at 4 and 1.5 at 3 all image at 1, all with H/Z = 0.5.

chain.zh: 于是看到一张像，只知道 H/Z：大而远和小而近分不出来。
chain.en: So an image tells only H/Z: big and far cannot be told from small and near.

naive.zh: 物高一样，像就一样高。
naive.en: Equal heights give equal images.

task.zh: 看一张图，判断关于场景的每句话：成立、不成立，还是无法确定；第二轮多知道一个物体的大小。
task.en: From one image, judge each statement about the scene: supported, contradicted or undetermined; the second round also knows one object's size.

question.zh: 一张图能确定场景里的哪些事，哪些不能？
question.en: What can one image settle about the scene, and what not?

chain.zh: 玩家按立方体在图里的大小读出它离相机 6 米、高 1 米，判为成立；判定画出另一个场景：放大一倍、推远一倍的立方体渲出同一张图。
chain.en: Reading off the cube's size in the image, the player calls it 6 m away and 1 m tall, supported; the judge draws another scene: a cube twice the size twice as far renders the same image.

chain.zh: 玩家把尺度歧义用到整个场景上：所有物体同比放大推远，图不变，所以距离和大小都定不了；颜色、个数在每个相容场景里都一样，定得了。
chain.en: The player applies scale ambiguity to the whole scene: every object scaled and pushed back together leaves the image unchanged, so distance and size are undetermined; colour and count are the same in every compatible scene, so settled.

chain.zh: 第二轮知道立方体边长 1 米：它的距离定下来了，球却仍可大可小，一个已知大小只定下它自己。
chain.en: In the second round the cube is known to be 1 m: its distance is settled, but the ball can still be bigger or smaller; a known size settles only its own object.

naive.zh: 从像的大小就能读出物体的距离和大小。
naive.en: An image's size tells how far and how big the object is.

task.zh: 光圈不动，只调透镜的对焦距离，让 4 m 处的门清晰。
task.en: With the aperture fixed, turn only the lens's focus distance so the door at 4 m is sharp.

question.zh: 透镜能让远处和近处同时清楚吗？
question.en: Can a lens make near and far sharp at once?

chain.zh: 玩家想两边都照顾，对焦在 2.5 m：检查后门和花的斑都超过门槛。
chain.en: To favour both, the player focuses at 2.5 m: checked, both the door's and the flower's spots are over the threshold.

chain.zh: 曲线显示斑只在对焦距离处缩成零，往两边越来越大：透镜只把一个距离收成点。
chain.en: The curve shows the spot shrinking to nothing only at the focus distance and growing either side: a lens brings one distance to points.

chain.zh: 对焦挪到门附近，门清晰了，花糊得更厉害。
chain.en: Focusing near the door makes it sharp and the flower blurs more.

naive.zh: 对焦在两个物体中间，两个都清楚。
naive.en: Focusing halfway makes both sharp.

task.zh: 对焦锁在 2 m 处的人身上，只调光圈：进光量至少 4，2.5 m 处的墙也清晰。
task.en: With the focus locked on a person at 2 m, turn only the aperture: the light at least 4 and the wall at 2.5 m sharp.

question.zh: 光圈开大有什么代价？
question.en: What does a wider aperture cost?

chain.zh: 玩家把光圈开到最大图亮：检查后墙的斑 0.05 mm，过了清晰门槛。
chain.en: The player opens fully for light: checked, the wall's spot is 0.05 mm, over the threshold.

chain.zh: 比较两档光圈：光圈加倍，墙的斑也加倍；斑的直径和光圈成正比。
chain.en: Comparing two apertures: double the aperture, double the wall's spot; its diameter is proportional to the aperture.

chain.zh: 进光量和 A² 成正比，至少要 A = 4；斑要在门槛内，A 不能超过 5。亮和清晰要互相让。
chain.en: Light goes as A², so A must be at least 4; for the spot to stay under the threshold A must not pass 5. Brightness and sharpness trade.

naive.zh: 光圈越大越好：只是更亮。
naive.en: The wider the better: it is only brighter.

task.zh: 同时调光圈和对焦距离：1 m 和 3 m 两个物体都清晰，进光量不低于 1。
task.en: Set the aperture and the focus together: objects at 1 m and 3 m both sharp, the light at least 1.

question.zh: 怎样让近处和远处同时清楚，又够亮？
question.en: How do near and far stay sharp together, with light enough?

chain.zh: 玩家对准近处的人、光圈开到够亮：曲线低于门槛的那一段围着 1 m，到不了 3 m。
chain.en: The player focuses on the near person with the aperture open enough: the stretch of the curve under the threshold surrounds 1 m and does not reach 3 m.

chain.zh: 收小光圈，这一段变长，可进光量跌到 1 以下；光圈最小只能 1.5 mm。
chain.en: Closing down lengthens the stretch, but the light falls below 1; the aperture can go no smaller than 1.5 mm.

chain.zh: 这一段在对焦距离两边都有：在 1.5 mm 光圈下把对焦挪到两者之间的 1.5 m，两边各盖住一个物体。
chain.en: The stretch reaches both sides of the focus: at 1.5 mm, moving the focus between them to 1.5 m covers one object on each side.

naive.zh: 对准其中一个、光圈开大就行。
naive.en: Focus on one of them and open the aperture.

task.zh: 手算一行放大后新像素在原图里的位置，再接出给出整张新图源坐标的电路。
task.en: Work out by hand where a row's new pixels sit in the original, then wire the circuit giving a whole new image's source coordinates.

question.zh: 放大一张图时，新像素的中心落在原图的哪里？
question.en: When an image is enlarged, where do the new pixels' centres fall in the original?

chain.zh: 玩家把 2 像素放大成 3 像素，写出 0、1、2：x = 2 在原图外面。
chain.en: Enlarging 2 pixels to 3, the player writes 0, 1, 2: x = 2 is outside the original.

chain.zh: 把新旧两排画成等长的两条：三个新像素中心分在两个旧像素占的长度上，落在 −1/6、0.5、7/6，中间那个在两个旧像素之间。
chain.en: Drawing the two rows as bars of one length: the three new centres spread over the length of the two old pixels, at −1/6, 0.5 and 7/6, the middle one between two old pixels.

chain.zh: 电路里每格先有自己的坐标，加 0.5 到中心，按宽度比例换算，再减 0.5 回到旧像素的下标。
chain.en: In the circuit every cell first gets its own coordinates, adds 0.5 to its centre, scales by the width ratio and takes 0.5 off to old pixel indices.

naive.zh: 新像素的下标就是原图的下标。
naive.en: A new pixel's index is its place in the original.

task.zh: 接出最近邻缩放：每个新像素照抄原图里离它最近的像素。
task.en: Wire nearest-neighbour resizing: each new pixel copies the original pixel nearest to it.

question.zh: 落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，最简单的取值办法是什么？
question.en: What is the simplest value for a new pixel between two old ones?

chain.zh: 采样网格给出的位置不是整数，取像素只收整数：玩家先把坐标向下取整。
chain.en: The sampling grid's positions are not whole numbers and the lookup takes only whole ones: the player rounds the coordinates down.

chain.zh: 测试里 [1, 2, 3, 4] 缩成 2 像素该得 [2, 4]，向下取整却给出 [1, 3]：0.5 向下取整是 0，可它离 1 和 0 一样近。
chain.en: A test wants [1, 2, 3, 4] shrunk to 2 pixels to give [2, 4]; rounding down gives [1, 3]: 0.5 rounds down to 0, though it is as near 1.

chain.zh: 最近的整数是加 0.5 再向下取整；放大后的图成块，新图里只有原图已有的值。
chain.en: The nearest whole number is add 0.5, then round down; enlarged, the image is blocky, holding only values the original had.

naive.zh: 坐标一律向下取整就是最近的那个。
naive.en: Rounding every coordinate down picks the nearest pixel.

task.zh: 手算一行按距离加权的放大，再接出一行像素的线性缩放电路。
task.en: Work out a row enlarged by distance-weighting by hand, then wire linear resizing of a row of pixels.

question.zh: 新像素一定要等于某一个旧像素吗？
question.en: Must a new pixel equal one of the old ones?

chain.zh: [0, 4] 放大成 4 像素，玩家照最近邻写出 [0, 0, 4, 4]：0.25 和 0.75 位置不同，值却一样。
chain.en: Enlarging [0, 4] to 4 pixels, the player writes [0, 0, 4, 4] by nearest neighbour: 0.25 and 0.75 sit apart but get the same value.

chain.zh: 按到两边的距离分配份量：0.25 处离 0 近，占 0.75 份，值是 1；0.75 处是 3。
chain.en: Sharing by distance: 0.25 is nearer 0, which takes 0.75 of it, giving 1; 0.75 gives 3.

chain.zh: 电路里向下取整得到左邻居，坐标减去它得到距离 t，值 = (1 − t) × 左 + t × 右。
chain.en: In the circuit, rounding down gives the left neighbour, the coordinate less it gives the distance t, and the value is (1 − t) × left + t × right.

naive.zh: 新像素只能照抄某一个旧像素。
naive.en: A new pixel can only copy an old one.

task.zh: 手算一张 2 × 2 的图放大成 3 × 3，再接出二维的双线性缩放电路。
task.en: Work out a 2 × 2 image enlarged to 3 × 3 by hand, then wire bilinear resizing in two dimensions.

question.zh: 新像素落在四个旧像素围成的方格里，值怎么算？
question.en: How is a new pixel among four old ones worked out?

chain.zh: 玩家只横着插值、竖直照抄最近的一行：中间一行落在两行正中，却整个抄了下面一行。
chain.en: Interpolating across only and copying the nearest row downwards, the player has the middle row, right between two, copy the lower one whole.

chain.zh: 竖直方向也有一个距离：先把上下两行各横着插值，再在两个结果之间竖着插一次，中心是四个邻居的平均 6。
chain.en: There is a vertical distance too: interpolate the top and bottom rows across, then between the two results downwards; the centre is the four neighbours' average, 6.

chain.zh: 展开来是四个邻居的加权平均，权重 (1−H)(1−V)、H(1−V)、(1−H)V、HV 加起来是 1。
chain.en: Expanded, it is a weighted average of the four, the weights (1−H)(1−V), H(1−V), (1−H)V and HV adding to 1.

naive.zh: 只横着插一次就够了。
naive.en: Interpolating across once is enough.

task.zh: 把按 BGR 存的照片换回 RGB：拆开每个像素的三个数，按新的顺序合成。
task.en: Turn a photo stored as BGR back to RGB: take each pixel's three numbers apart and compose them in the new order.

question.zh: 为什么用 OpenCV 读进来的照片，天是橙色的？
question.en: Why is the sky orange in a photo read with OpenCV?

chain.zh: 玩家把输入原样接到输出：第一个格子里第 0 和第 2 个数对调了。
chain.en: The player wires the input straight to the output: in the first cell the numbers at positions 0 and 2 are swapped.

chain.zh: 分别取出三个位置看，天空最亮的在位置 0：这张图第 0 个数是蓝。
chain.en: Taking the three positions out one by one, the sky is brightest at position 0: this image's first number is blue.

chain.zh: 按 R、G、B 的顺序取位置 2、1、0 合成，颜色就回来了。
chain.en: Composing positions 2, 1, 0 as R, G, B brings the colours back.

naive.zh: 三个数总是 R、G、B。
naive.en: The three numbers are always R, G, B.

question.zh: 一张图从哪里来、能说明什么，图里的像素又怎样重新采样？
question.en: Where does an image come from, what can it tell, and how are its pixels resampled?

title.en: An image does not settle depth

value.zh: 三条梯子，各从一个浅显的起点爬到第 1、2 讲的一个核心：一张图为什么定不了深度，透镜怎样在亮和清晰之间取舍，缩放时新像素怎样从四个邻居算出。
value.en: Three ladders, each climbing from a plain starting point to a core of lectures 1–2: why one image cannot settle depth, how a lens trades light against sharpness, and how resizing works a new pixel out of four neighbours.

body.zh: 针孔相机里，物点发出的光只有穿过小孔的那一条落到像平面上：像点在物点和小孔连成的直线上，横向位置 u = fX/Z。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 11）。常见的误解：像就落在和物点同样的横向位置上（u = X）。
body.en: In a pinhole camera only the ray through the hole reaches the image plane: the image of a point lies on the line through the point and the hole, at u = fX/Z. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 11). A common mistake: The image lands at the point's own lateral position (u = X).

body.zh: 物体的像高 h = fH/Z：和距离成反比，距离加倍，像缩成一半。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 9–11）。常见的误解：距离每多一点，像就少同样多一点（按差来减）。
body.en: An object's image height is h = fH/Z: inversely proportional to the distance; twice as far, half as tall. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 9–11). A common mistake: Each step farther takes the same amount off the image (a difference, not a ratio).

body.zh: 物高和距离同比放大，像一点不变：一张像只定下物高和距离的比值 H/Z。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 9–11）。常见的误解：物高一样，像就一样高。
body.en: Scale an object's size and distance by the same factor and its image does not change: an image fixes only the ratio H/Z. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 9–11). A common mistake: Equal heights give equal images.

body.zh: 图形学由场景生成图像；视觉反过来，从图像推回场景。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲（幻灯片 8）。
body.en: Graphics makes an image from a scene; vision goes the other way, from an image back to a scene. Source: COMP90086 lecture 1 (slide 8).

body.zh: 从图像推回场景时，常有不止一个场景给出同一张图：投影把深度丢掉了。一张图能确定的只是所有相容场景都同意的事；其余要靠另外的线索（已知的物体大小、第二台相机……）。出处：COMP90086 第 1 讲（幻灯片 8）。常见的误解：从像的大小就能读出物体的距离和大小。
body.en: Going from an image back to a scene, more than one scene often gives the same image: projection drops depth. An image settles only what every compatible scene agrees on; the rest needs other cues (a known size, a second camera…). Source: COMP90086 lecture 1 (slide 8). A common mistake: An image's size tells how far and how big the object is.

body.zh: 透镜把一大片光收拢，可只能把一个距离上的点收成点；别的距离上的点落成一块斑。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 12–13）。常见的误解：对焦在两个物体中间，两个都清楚。
body.en: A lens gathers much more light, but brings the points of only one distance to points; points at other distances land as spots. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slides 12–13). A common mistake: Focusing halfway makes both sharp.

body.zh: 离焦的点在传感器上落成一块圆斑；光圈越大，进光越多，这块斑也越大。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 16）。常见的误解：光圈越大越好：只是更亮。
body.en: An out-of-focus point lands on the sensor as a round spot; the wider the aperture, the more light and the bigger the spot. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 16). A common mistake: The wider the better: it is only brighter.

body.zh: 斑小到眼睛（或一个像素）分不出来，就算清楚。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 16）。
body.en: A spot too small for the eye (or a pixel) to tell from a point counts as sharp. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 16).

body.zh: 对焦距离前后，模糊圈还小于容许模糊圈的那一段距离。光圈越小，斑长得越慢，这一段越长，可进光也越少。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 16）。常见的误解：对准其中一个、光圈开大就行。
body.en: The range of distances around the focus where the blur circle stays within the acceptable blur. A smaller aperture grows the spot more slowly and lengthens the range, at the cost of light. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 16). A common mistake: Focus on one of them and open the aperture.

body.zh: 缩放时，新图每个像素的中心按比例落回原图：新旧两排像素占同样长的一段，新像素中心常落在两个旧像素之间。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 34）。常见的误解：新像素的下标就是原图的下标。
body.en: When resizing, each new pixel's centre maps back into the original in proportion: both rows span the same length, so new centres often fall between old pixels. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 34). A common mistake: A new pixel's index is its place in the original.

body.zh: 每个新像素照抄离它最近的旧像素：快、边缘硬，放大后成块。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 35）。常见的误解：坐标一律向下取整就是最近的那个。
body.en: Each new pixel copies the nearest old pixel: fast and hard-edged, blocky when enlarged. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 35). A common mistake: Rounding every coordinate down picks the nearest pixel.

body.zh: 新像素按它到两个邻居的距离加权：离谁近，谁的份量大；正中间就是两者的平均。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 36）。常见的误解：新像素只能照抄某一个旧像素。
body.en: A new pixel weighs its two neighbours by distance: the nearer counts more; halfway is their average. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 36). A common mistake: A new pixel can only copy an old one.

body.zh: 新像素落在四个旧像素之间时，先横着做两次线性插值，再竖着做一次：四个邻居的加权平均，权重 (1−H)(1−V)、H(1−V)、(1−H)V、HV 加起来是 1。比最近邻平滑，会让锐利的边稍微变软。出处：COMP90086 第 2 讲（幻灯片 36）。常见的误解：只横着插一次就够了。
body.en: A new pixel among four old ones is two linear interpolations across, then one down: a weighted average of the four, the weights (1−H)(1−V), H(1−V), (1−H)V, HV adding to 1. Smoother than nearest neighbour; it softens sharp edges a little. Source: COMP90086 lecture 2 (slide 36). A common mistake: Interpolating across once is enough.

body.zh: 彩色像素的三个数按什么顺序存是约定：OpenCV 读进来的是 B、G、R，Matplotlib 显示时当成 R、G、B，不换就红蓝颠倒。出处：COMP90086 第 2 次 workshop。常见的误解：三个数总是 R、G、B。
body.en: The order a colour pixel's three numbers are stored in is a convention: OpenCV reads B, G, R, Matplotlib shows R, G, B; without a swap red and blue trade places. Source: COMP90086 workshop 2. A common mistake: The three numbers are always R, G, B.

t.zh: 相机台上是一台理想的针孔相机：场景里一点发出的光，只有穿过小孔的那一条落到像平面上。像平面离小孔 f，点离小孔 Z、偏离光轴 X；台上把像平面画在小孔前面，像是正的。
t.en: The bench holds an ideal pinhole camera: of all the light a scene point sends out, only the ray through the hole reaches the image plane. The plane is f from the hole, the point Z away and X off the axis; the bench draws the plane in front of the hole, so the image is upright.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：一点放在哪里，它的像才落在像平面上画圈的位置？两个任务各开一个旋钮：先横向移动这一点，再前后移动它。先想好放在哪里再按「检查」，检查之后才画出光线和像；像落进圆圈才算对。
t.en: This level asks: where must a point be for its image to land on the circled spot of the image plane? Each of the two tasks opens one knob: first move the point sideways, then in depth. Decide where to put it before you press Check; the ray and the image are drawn only once you check. It is right when the image lands in the circle.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="central-projection"></wiki-ref>：像点在物点和小孔的连线上，u = fX/Z。物点离得越远，同样的横向偏移在像上越小。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="central-projection"></wiki-ref>: the image lies on the line through the point and the hole, u = fX/Z. The farther the point, the smaller the same sideways offset becomes in the image.

brief.zh: f = 2，点离小孔 Z = 4：横向移动这一点，让它的像落在 u = 1。
brief.en: f = 2, the point Z = 4 from the hole: move it sideways so its image lands at u = 1.

hint.zh: 顺着画出的光线看：它从点出发，穿过小孔，停在像平面上。像平面离小孔多远，点又离小孔多远？
hint.en: Follow the drawn ray from the point through the hole to the plane. How far is the plane from the hole, and the point?

why.zh: 把点放在 X = 1，像却只落到 u = 0.5：光线穿过小孔后，横向位置按 f/Z = 2/4 缩小了一半。
why.en: With the point at X = 1 the image lands at u = 0.5 only: through the hole, the sideways position shrinks by f/Z = 2/4, to half.

brief.zh: f = 2，点偏离光轴 X = 2：只前后移动它，让像落在 u = 0.5。
brief.en: f = 2, the point X = 2 off the axis: move it only in depth so its image lands at u = 0.5.

hint.zh: Z = 2 时像在 u = 2。退到两倍远，像挪到哪里？要挪到四分之一呢？
hint.en: At Z = 2 the image is at u = 2. Twice as far, where does it go? To get a quarter of that?

why.zh: 退到两倍远，像只挪到 u = 1：像的位置和距离成反比，要到 u = 0.5，得退到四倍远。
why.en: Twice as far, the image moves only to u = 1: its position is inversely proportional to the distance, so u = 0.5 needs four times as far.

t.zh: 一支竖着的箭从光轴立起，高 H。箭的两端各有一条光线穿过小孔，两条线在像平面上截出的那一段，就是箭的像，高 h。
t.en: An upright arrow stands H tall on the axis. A ray from each end passes the hole, and the stretch the two rays cut out of the image plane is the arrow's image, h tall.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：物体离得越远，像矮多少？换一支镜头，像又高多少？第一个任务只能前后移动箭，第二个任务箭不动，只能调像平面到小孔的距离 f。像高等于圆圈标出的高度才算对；先想好，再按「检查」。
t.en: This level asks: how much shorter does an image get as the object moves away, and how much taller with another lens? The first task moves only the arrow in depth; in the second the arrow stays and only f, the plane's distance from the hole, turns. It is right when the image is as tall as the circled mark; decide first, then press Check.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="perspective-scaling"></wiki-ref>：像高 h = fH/Z，和距离成反比、和 f 成正比。距离加倍，像缩成一半；不是每远一点就少同样一截。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="perspective-scaling"></wiki-ref>: the image height h = fH/Z, inversely proportional to distance and proportional to f. Twice as far, half as tall; not the same amount off for each step back.

brief.zh: 箭高 H = 2，f = 2：只前后移动箭，让像高 h = 1。
brief.en: The arrow H = 2 tall, f = 2: move it only in depth so its image is h = 1 tall.

hint.zh: Z = 2 时像和箭一样高。像要变成一半，距离要怎样变？
hint.en: At Z = 2 the image is as tall as the arrow. For half that, how must the distance change?

why.zh: 以为距离多 1，像就矮 1：Z = 3 时像高是 1.33。像高按 1/Z 变，要矮一半，距离得加倍。
why.en: Taking one step back for one unit off the image: at Z = 3 it is 1.33 tall. Height goes as 1/Z; half as tall needs twice as far.

brief.zh: 箭高 H = 2，离小孔 Z = 8：箭不动，只调 f，让像高 h = 0.75。
brief.en: The arrow H = 2 tall, Z = 8 away: leave it there and turn only f, so its image is h = 0.75 tall.

hint.zh: f = 1 时像高 0.25。要三倍高，f 要怎样变？
hint.en: At f = 1 the image is 0.25 tall. Three times as tall needs what f?

why.zh: 以为差多少补多少：f 加 0.5，像高只到 0.375。像高和 f 成正比，要三倍高，f 也要三倍。
why.en: Adding what is missing: f up by 0.5 brings the image only to 0.375. Height is proportional to f; three times as tall needs three times f.

t.zh: 到这里，任务都是由物体求像。反过来：看到一个像有多高，能说出物体多高、多远吗？
t.en: So far every task has gone from the object to its image. The other way round: from how tall an image is, can you tell how tall and how far the object is?

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：哪些物体会成一样高的像？f = 2，每一轮给出几组（物高, 距离），选出至少两组：每组的像高都是 1，距离各不相同。
t.en: This level asks: which objects image equally tall? With f = 2, each round lists several (height, distance) pairs; choose at least two that all image 1 tall, no two at the same distance.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="scale-ambiguity"></wiki-ref>：物高和距离同比放大，像一点不变。一张像只定下 H/Z，大而远和小而近分不出来。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="scale-ambiguity"></wiki-ref>: scale an object's height and distance together and its image does not change. An image fixes only H/Z; big and far cannot be told from small and near.

brief.zh: f = 2：选出像高都是 1、距离各不相同的两组以上。
brief.en: f = 2: choose two or more pairs that all image 1 tall, at different distances.

hint.zh: 像高 h = fH/Z。物高和距离一起翻倍，h 怎样变？
hint.en: The image height is h = fH/Z. When height and distance both double, what happens to h?

prompt.zh: 哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: Which pairs all image 1 tall, at different distances?

prompt.zh: 换一批：哪几组的像高都是 1、距离又各不相同？
prompt.en: Another set: which pairs all image 1 tall, at different distances?

why.zh: 挑了一样高的物体：可像高还取决于距离，高 2 的箱子在距离 2 处成的像高 2。成一样高的像的，是 H/Z 相同的那些。
why.en: That picks objects of one height, but the image also depends on distance: the crate 2 tall at distance 2 images 2 tall. Equal images come from equal H/Z.

t.zh: 画一张图是由场景到图像：物体、光照、相机都给定，图就定了，这是<wiki-ref to="graphics-vision"></wiki-ref>里图形学的方向。视觉走反方向，手里只有图，要说出场景是什么样。
t.en: Drawing goes from scene to image: given the objects, the light and the camera, the image is settled; that is the graphics side of <wiki-ref to="graphics-vision"></wiki-ref>. Vision goes the other way: it holds only the image and must say what the scene is like.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：只看一张图，场景里哪些事能确定，哪些确定不了？每一轮给一张图，判断关于场景的每句话：凡是渲得出这张图的场景里它都成立，选「成立」；都不成立，选「不成立」；有的场景成立、有的不成立，选「无法确定」。第二轮多给了一条线索。
t.en: This level asks: from one image alone, what about the scene can be settled and what cannot? Each round gives an image; judge each statement about the scene: true in every scene that renders this image, Supported; false in all of them, Contradicted; true in some and false in others, Undetermined. The second round gives one more cue.

after.zh: 从图推回场景是<wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>：投影把深度丢了，大而远和小而近渲出同一张图。图能确定的只是所有相容场景都同意的事（颜色、个数）；距离和大小要另外的线索，比如一个已知大小的物体，而它也只定下自己的距离。
after.en: Going from an image back to a scene is an <wiki-ref to="inverse-problem"></wiki-ref>: projection drops depth, and big-and-far renders the same image as small-and-near. An image settles only what every compatible scene agrees on (colour, count); distance and size need another cue, such as an object of known size, and that settles only its own distance.

brief.zh: 判断关于场景的每句话：成立、不成立，还是无法确定。
brief.en: Judge each statement about the scene: supported, contradicted, or undetermined.

hint.zh: 立方体在图里的大小，取决于它有多大，也取决于它有多远。把它放大一倍、再推远一倍，图会变吗？
hint.en: The cube's size in the image depends on how big it is and how far. Double its size and its distance: does the image change?

hint.zh: 第二轮知道了立方体的边长：它的距离定下来了；球的呢？
hint.en: In the second round the cube's side is known: that settles its distance; what about the ball's?

prompt.zh: 红色立方体离相机 6 米。
prompt.en: The red cube is 6 m from the camera.

prompt.zh: 球是蓝色的。
prompt.en: The ball is blue.

prompt.zh: 场景里有两个球。
prompt.en: The scene has two balls.

prompt.zh: 立方体高 1 米。
prompt.en: The cube is 1 m tall.

prompt.zh: 已知立方体边长 1 米。立方体离相机 6 米。
prompt.en: The cube is known to be 1 m on a side. The cube is 6 m from the camera.

prompt.zh: 球离相机 6.5 米。
prompt.en: The ball is 6.5 m from the camera.

prompt.zh: 球的直径是 0.6 米。
prompt.en: The ball is 0.6 m across.

prompt.zh: 立方体是红色的。
prompt.en: The cube is red.

why.zh: 按物体在图里的大小读出了一个距离和一个大小：可放大一倍又推远一倍的场景渲出同一张图。知道立方体有多大，只定下立方体的距离，球仍然可大可小、可远可近。
why.en: That reads one distance and one size off how big the objects look, but a scene scaled up and pushed back as much renders the same image. Knowing the cube's size settles only the cube's distance; the ball can still be bigger and farther or smaller and nearer.

t.zh: 针孔只放进一条光线，图很暗；把孔开大，同一点的光落到传感器上一大片，图就糊。相机在孔的位置装一块焦距 50 mm 的透镜：它把从一点射来的一大束光重新收拢成一点。收拢在哪里，取决于这一点有多远；转动对焦，就是挪动传感器去接住某个距离上收拢的点。
t.en: A pinhole lets in one ray and the image is dark; widen the hole and one point's light spreads over the sensor, and the image blurs. A camera puts a 50 mm lens where the hole was: it gathers a wide beam from a point back into a point. Where that happens depends on how far the point is; turning the focus moves the sensor to catch the points of one distance.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：透镜能让近处和远处同时清晰吗？台上有 1 m 处的花和 4 m 处的门，光圈固定。只调对焦距离，让远处的门清晰：它在传感器上的斑不超过清晰门槛 0.03 mm。先想好再按「检查」，检查之后才画出光线和每个深度的斑。
t.en: This level asks: can a lens make near and far sharp at once? The bench holds a flower at 1 m and a door at 4 m; the aperture is fixed. Turn only the focus distance so the far door is sharp: its spot on the sensor no wider than the 0.03 mm threshold. Decide before you press Check; only then are the rays and each depth's spot drawn.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="focus"></wiki-ref>：透镜只把对焦距离上的点收成点，别的距离上的点落成一块斑。对焦在两者中间，两个都不清晰。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="focus"></wiki-ref>: a lens brings only the points at the focus distance to points; points at other distances land as spots. Focused halfway, neither is sharp.

brief.zh: 光圈不动，只调对焦距离：让 4 m 处的门清晰。
brief.en: With the aperture fixed, turn only the focus distance: make the door at 4 m sharp.

hint.zh: 透镜把哪个距离上的点收成点？
hint.en: Which distance does the lens bring to points?

why.zh: 对焦在两者中间，想两个都照顾到：门的斑有 0.04 mm，花的更大，两个都不清晰。透镜只把一个距离收成点。
why.en: Focusing halfway to favour both: the door's spot is 0.04 mm and the flower's larger, so neither is sharp. A lens brings one distance to points.

t.zh: 光圈直径 A 管进来多少光：进光量和 A² 成正比，这里以 2 mm 光圈的进光为 1。离焦的点落成的斑有一个还算清晰的上限，台上的清晰门槛 0.03 mm 就是<wiki-ref to="acceptable-blur"></wiki-ref>：斑小到分不出是不是一个点，就算清晰。
t.en: The aperture diameter A sets how much light comes in: light goes as A², counted here against a 2 mm aperture as 1. The spot an out-of-focus point makes has a limit below which it still counts as sharp; the bench's 0.03 mm threshold is the <wiki-ref to="acceptable-blur"></wiki-ref>: a spot too small to tell from a point is sharp.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：光圈开大，除了更亮，还换来了什么？对焦锁在 2 m 处的人身上，身后 2.5 m 是一面墙。只调光圈：进光量至少 4，墙也要清晰。先想好再按「检查」。
t.en: This level asks: a wider aperture is brighter; what else does it bring? The focus is locked on a person at 2 m, with a wall behind them at 2.5 m. Turn only the aperture: the light at least 4, and the wall sharp too. Decide before you press Check.

after.zh: 离焦的点落成的斑叫<wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref>：它的直径和光圈成正比。光圈开大，光多了，斑也大了；亮和清晰要互相让。
after.en: The spot an out-of-focus point makes is its <wiki-ref to="blur-circle"></wiki-ref>: its diameter is proportional to the aperture. Open up and there is more light, and bigger spots; brightness and sharpness trade against each other.

brief.zh: 对焦锁在 2 m：只调光圈，进光量至少 4，2.5 m 处的墙清晰。
brief.en: Focus locked at 2 m: turn only the aperture, with the light at least 4 and the wall at 2.5 m sharp.

hint.zh: 检查过一档光圈后，看墙的斑：光圈加倍，斑变成多大？
hint.en: Once one aperture is checked, look at the wall's spot: double the aperture, how big does it get?

hint.zh: 进光量和 A² 成正比：要到 4，A 至少多大？
hint.en: Light goes as A²: what A gives at least 4?

why.zh: 光圈开到最大，只当它更亮：进光量 25，墙的斑却有 0.05 mm，超过了门槛。斑的直径随光圈一起长。
why.en: Opening fully, as if it only brightened: the light is 25, but the wall's spot is 0.05 mm, over the threshold. The spot grows with the aperture.

t.zh: 对焦距离上的点收成点，前后的点落成斑，斑随着离开对焦距离越来越大。斑还在清晰门槛以下的那一段距离，前后都算清晰。
t.en: Points at the focus distance come to points; points before and behind land as spots that grow the farther they are from it. The stretch of distances where the spot stays under the threshold counts as sharp.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：近处和远处都要清晰，又要够亮，光圈和对焦各放在哪里？1 m 处的人和 3 m 处的门都要清晰，进光量（以 1.5 mm 光圈为 1）不低于 1。光圈和对焦都能调；先想好再按「检查」，检查后才画出斑随深度变化的曲线。
t.en: This level asks: with near and far both to be sharp and light enough, where do the aperture and the focus go? A person at 1 m and a door at 3 m must both be sharp, and the light (a 1.5 mm aperture counting as 1) at least 1. Both the aperture and the focus turn; decide before you press Check, and only then is the curve of spot size against depth drawn.

after.zh: 斑小于容许模糊圈的那一段距离叫<wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>。光圈越小，斑长得越慢，这一段越长，可光越少；它在对焦距离两边都有，对焦放在中间才用得上两边。
after.en: The range of distances where the spot stays within the acceptable blur is the <wiki-ref to="depth-of-field"></wiki-ref>. A smaller aperture grows the spot more slowly and lengthens it, at the cost of light; it reaches both sides of the focus, so focusing between the two uses both.

brief.zh: 同时调光圈和对焦距离：1 m 和 3 m 都清晰，进光量不低于 1。
brief.en: Set the aperture and the focus together: 1 m and 3 m both sharp, the light at least 1.

hint.zh: 对焦在一个物体上时，清晰的那一段有一边落在两个物体外面，用不上。
hint.en: Focused on one of the objects, one side of the sharp stretch lies beyond both of them, unused.

hint.zh: 光圈不能小于 1.5 mm：在这个光圈下，对焦挪到哪里，清晰的一段刚好盖住两个物体？
hint.en: The aperture cannot go under 1.5 mm: at that aperture, where must the focus go for the sharp stretch to cover both?

why.zh: 对准近处的人、光圈开到够亮：清晰的一段从 1 m 往两边伸，到不了 3 m，门糊了。
why.en: Focusing on the near person with the aperture open enough: the sharp stretch spreads both ways from 1 m and does not reach 3 m; the door blurs.

why.zh: 对焦放对了，光圈却开得更大：斑长得快，清晰的一段缩短，两头都出了界。
why.en: The focus is right, but the aperture wider: the spots grow faster, the sharp stretch shortens and both ends fall outside it.

t.zh: 把一张图放大或缩小，新图的每个像素都要有一个值；算值之前，先得知道这个像素落在原图的什么位置。约定是：新旧两排像素占同样长的一段，像素的中心对齐到这段长度上。
t.en: Enlarging or shrinking an image gives every pixel of the new image a value; before any value, each must know where it sits in the original. The convention: the old and the new row span one length, and pixel centres are spread over it.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：缩放时，新图的每个像素落在原图的哪里？第一个任务在格子上手算一行；第二个任务接一块电路，交出整张新图的两张源坐标图，测试的坐标都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: when an image is resized, where in the original does each new pixel sit? The first task works out one row by hand on the grid; the second wires a circuit that gives the whole new image's two source-coordinate images, right when every tested coordinate is.

desc.zh: 输入原图的宽 sw、高 sh 和新图的宽 nw、高 nh，输出新图每个像素在原图里的 x、y（两张坐标图）
desc.en: Takes the original's width sw and height sh and the new width nw and height nh; gives each new pixel's x and y in the original (two coordinate images)

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>：每个新像素反向映射回原图，落点一般不在旧像素的中心上，常在两个旧像素之间。
after.en: This is a <wiki-ref to="sampling-grid"></wiki-ref>: each new pixel mapped back into the original, landing seldom on an old pixel's centre and often between two.

brief.zh: 这一行 2 像素宽，放大成 3 像素：写出每个新像素在原图里的 x。
brief.en: This row, 2 pixels wide, is enlarged to 3: write where each new pixel sits in the original, as x.

hint.zh: 把新旧两排画成等长的两条，各自的像素中心落在哪里？
hint.en: Draw the two rows as two bars of one length: where does each pixel centre fall?

after.zh: 新像素不是旧像素换了编号：中间那个落在两个旧像素之间。
after.en: New pixels are not old ones renumbered: the middle one falls between two old pixels.

label.zh: 新像素在原图里的 x

why.zh: 这是把新像素当成旧像素重新编号：原图这一行只有 x = 0 和 x = 1 两个像素，x = 2 落在原图外面。新旧两排一样长，三个新像素中心要分布在两个旧像素占的那段长度上。
why.en: That renumbers the new pixels as if they were old ones: the original row has pixels at x = 0 and x = 1 only, so x = 2 lies outside it. The two rows are equally long, so the three new centres spread over the length the two old pixels cover.

t.zh: 手算一行可以，一整张图要每个像素各算一遍，就要电路了：输入从左边进来，输出从右边出去。新图的每个像素先要有自己的坐标，而手上没有元件能从两个数造出一整张图。
t.en: One row works by hand; a whole image, every pixel worked out, needs a circuit: inputs come in on the left, outputs leave on the right. Each new pixel first needs its own coordinates, and nothing in hand makes a whole image out of two numbers.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref>给定宽和高，给出每格就是自己 x、y 的两张坐标图。坐标还要换算：<part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref>给出一个固定的数，<part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref>、<part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref>对数和整张图逐个值地算。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:grid"></part-ref> takes a width and a height and gives the two coordinate images whose cells hold their own x and y. The coordinates still need converting: <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref> gives a fixed number, and <part-ref to="part:add"></part-ref>, <part-ref to="part:mul"></part-ref> and <part-ref to="part:div"></part-ref> work value by value on numbers and whole images.

brief.zh: 输入原图和新图的宽高：交出新图每个像素在原图里的 x 坐标图和 y 坐标图。
brief.en: Given the original's and the new width and height, give the image of each new pixel's x in the original, and the image of its y.

hint.zh: 先给新图的每个像素一对它自己的坐标。
hint.en: First give every pixel of the new image its own pair of coordinates.

hint.zh: 新图的一个像素宽，相当于原图的几个像素宽？像素中心和像素左边差多少？
hint.en: One pixel of the new image is how many pixels of the original wide? How far is a pixel's centre from its left edge?

t.zh: 有了<part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref>，每个新像素都知道自己落在原图的哪里；可这个位置一般不是整数，原图在那里没有像素。
t.en: With the <part-ref to="sampleGrid"></part-ref> every new pixel knows where it sits in the original; but that position is seldom a whole number, and the original has no pixel there.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：落在两个旧像素之间的新像素，最简单的取值办法是什么？新元件<part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref>按整数坐标在图上取值，<part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref>读出图的宽高，<part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref>把一个数向下取整。离两边一样远时，约定取坐标较大的一边。输出图逐格和期望相符才算对。
t.en: This level asks: what is the simplest value for a new pixel between two old ones? New parts: <part-ref to="part:lookup"></part-ref> reads an image at whole-number coordinates, <part-ref to="part:size"></part-ref> gives an image's width and height, and <part-ref to="part:floor"></part-ref> rounds a number down. When a position is equally far from two pixels, the convention takes the larger coordinate. It is right when the output matches the expected image cell by cell.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>：每个新像素照抄离它最近的旧像素。快、边缘硬，放大后成块，新图里只有原图已有的值。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="nearest-neighbour"></wiki-ref>: each new pixel copies the nearest old one. Fast and hard-edged, blocky when enlarged, with no value the original did not already have.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素照抄原图里离它最近的那个像素。
brief.en: Given an image and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel copying the original pixel nearest to it.

hint.zh: 取像素只接受整数坐标，也不接受原图外面的坐标。
hint.en: The lookup takes only whole-number coordinates, and none outside the image.

hint.zh: 离一个坐标最近的整数，和它向下取整得到的整数，什么时候不一样？
hint.en: When does the whole number nearest a coordinate differ from the one rounding down gives?

t.zh: 最近邻只会照抄：[0, 4] 放大成 4 像素，新像素不是 0 就是 4。可中间的新像素离两边的距离不一样，照抄丢掉了这个信息。
t.en: Nearest neighbour only copies: [0, 4] enlarged to 4 pixels gives every new pixel 0 or 4. Yet the middle ones sit at different distances from the two sides, and copying throws that away.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：新像素一定要等于某一个旧像素吗？先在格子上手算一行，再接一块电路：输入一行像素和新的宽、高，交出缩放后的图。这一关的图都只有一行；测试和隐藏测试的每个值都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: must a new pixel equal one of the old ones? First work one row out by hand on the grid, then wire a circuit: given a row of pixels and a new width and height, give the resized image. This level's images are all one row high; it is right when every value in the tests and hidden tests is.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：新像素按到左右两个旧像素的距离加权，离谁近谁的份量大，两份权重加起来是 1。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="linear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: a new pixel weighs its left and right neighbours by distance, the nearer counting more, the two weights adding to 1.

brief.zh: [0, 4] 放大成 4 像素：新像素落在 x = −0.25、0.25、0.75、1.25。按到两边旧像素的距离，写出每个新像素的值；落在两端外面的，取最近的边。
brief.en: [0, 4] enlarged to 4 pixels: the new pixels sit at x = −0.25, 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25. Write each one's value by its distance to the old pixels on either side; one beyond an end takes the nearest edge.

hint.zh: x = 0.25 离 x = 0 有 0.25，离 x = 1 有 0.75。离得近的那一边该占几成？
hint.en: x = 0.25 is 0.25 from x = 0 and 0.75 from x = 1. What share should the nearer side take?

why.zh: 这是照抄最近的旧像素：x = 0.25 和 x = 0.75 落在不同的位置，却拿到一样的值。按距离加权，0.25 处是 0.75 × 0 + 0.25 × 4 = 1。
why.en: That copies the nearest old pixel: x = 0.25 and x = 0.75 sit at different places but get one value each side. Weighted by distance, 0.25 gives 0.75 × 0 + 0.25 × 4 = 1.

brief.zh: 输入一行像素和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素由左右两个旧像素按距离加权。
brief.en: Given a row of pixels and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel weighted from its left and right old pixels by distance.

hint.zh: 中间那个新像素离左右两个旧像素各有多远？
hint.en: How far is the middle new pixel from each of the two old ones?

hint.zh: 先找出新位置左边那个旧像素，再算新位置离它有多远。
hint.en: First find the old pixel to the left of the new position, then how far the position is from it.

hint.zh: 两端的新位置落在原图之外：取像素可以设成取最近的边。
hint.en: The new positions at the ends fall outside the original: the lookup can be set to read the nearest edge.

t.zh: 一行像素之间，新像素按左右两个邻居加权。放大一张二维的图，新像素在上下方向也落在两行之间：它周围有四个旧像素。
t.en: Within a row, a new pixel weighs its left and right neighbours. Enlarging a 2D image, a new pixel also falls between two rows: there are four old pixels around it.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：落在四个旧像素围成的方格里的新像素，值怎么算？先在格子上手算一张 2 × 2 的图放大成 3 × 3，再接一块电路：输入一张图和新的宽、高，交出缩放后的图，二维放大和缩小的测试都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: how is a new pixel inside the square of four old ones worked out? First work a 2 × 2 image enlarged to 3 × 3 by hand on the grid, then wire a circuit: given an image and a new width and height, give the resized image, right when the tests of enlarging and shrinking in two dimensions all are.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>：上下两行各沿 x 插一次，再沿 y 在两个结果之间插一次，等于四个邻居的加权平均，权重加起来是 1。它比最近邻平滑，也会让锐利的边稍微变软。
after.en: This is <wiki-ref to="bilinear-interpolation"></wiki-ref>: interpolate along x on the row above and the row below, then along y between the two results; that is a weighted average of the four neighbours, the weights adding to 1. Smoother than nearest neighbour, it also softens sharp edges a little.

brief.zh: 这张 2 × 2 的图放大成 3 × 3：新像素的 x、y 都落在 −1/6、0.5、7/6。写出 3 × 3 的值；落在外面的取最近的边。
brief.en: This 2 × 2 image is enlarged to 3 × 3: the new pixels' x and y both fall at −1/6, 0.5 and 7/6. Write the 3 × 3 values; positions outside take the nearest edge.

hint.zh: 中间那一行落在 y = 0.5，正好在两行中间：它该等于哪一行？
hint.en: The middle row falls at y = 0.5, right between the two rows: which row should it equal?

hint.zh: 先把上下两行各自横着放大，再在两行之间竖着取。
hint.en: Enlarge the top and bottom rows across first, then take between the two rows downwards.

why.zh: 只横着插了一次，竖直方向照抄最近的一行：中间一行落在两行正中，却整个抄了下面那一行。竖着也按距离加权，中心是四个邻居的平均 6。
why.en: That interpolates across only and copies the nearest row downwards: the middle row, right between the two, copies the lower one whole. Weighted by distance downwards too, the centre is the four neighbours' average, 6.

brief.zh: 输入一张图和新的宽、高：交出缩放后的图，每个新像素由周围四个旧像素按距离加权。
brief.en: Given an image and a new width and height, give the resized image, each new pixel weighted from the four old pixels around it by distance.

hint.zh: 竖直方向也有一个距离：新位置离上面那一行有多远。
hint.en: There is a vertical distance too: how far the new position is from the row above.

hint.zh: 上下两行各沿 x 插一次，得到两个值，再在它们之间沿 y 插一次。
hint.en: Interpolate along x on the row above and on the row below, then along y between the two results.

t.zh: 彩色图的每个像素存三个数，各是哪种颜色，看存的顺序。OpenCV 读进来的照片按 B、G、R 存；拿去按 R、G、B 显示，红和蓝就对调了：一张蓝天的照片显示出橙色的天空。
t.en: A colour image stores three numbers a pixel, and which colour each is depends on the order they are stored in. A photo read with OpenCV is stored as B, G, R; shown as R, G, B, red and blue trade places, and a blue sky shows orange.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：怎样把这张照片的颜色换回来？新元件<part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref>取出每个像素第 0、1 或 2 个位置上的数（在元件上设定），组成一张灰度图；<part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref>把三张灰度图依次当作 R、G、B，合成一张彩色图。每个像素都和期望相符才算对。
t.en: This level asks: how do you put the photo's colours back? New parts: <part-ref to="part:channel"></part-ref> takes the number at position 0, 1 or 2 of every pixel, as set on the part, as a grey image; <part-ref to="part:compose"></part-ref> takes three grey images as R, G and B, in that order, and makes one colour image. It is right when every pixel matches the expected one.

after.zh: 这是<wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>的差别：OpenCV 按 BGR 存，Matplotlib 按 RGB 显示，交给另一个库之前要把顺序换过来。
after.en: This is a difference of <wiki-ref to="channel-order"></wiki-ref>: OpenCV stores BGR and Matplotlib shows RGB, so the order must be swapped before one hands an image to the other.

brief.zh: 输入是用 OpenCV 读进来的照片：交出同一张照片，颜色和本来的一样。
brief.en: The input is a photo read with OpenCV: give the same photo in its true colours.

hint.zh: 先把输入原样接到输出，看第一个不同的格子里哪几个数对调了。
hint.en: First wire the input straight to the output, and see which numbers are swapped in the first differing cell.

hint.zh: 把三个位置的数分别取出来看：天空在哪一张里最亮？蓝天本该亮在哪一种颜色上？
hint.en: Take the numbers at the three positions out one by one: in which of them is the sky brightest? Which colour should a blue sky be bright in?

step.why: A demonstration course: three ladders to the cores of lectures 1–2, and one optional technical topic

t.zh: 整台机器从一台视觉检查台起步。它不会计算，也碰不到一个像素：它只看图，读别的视觉系统交出的输出，判断哪一份回答了请求。同一张图上能提的问题不止一种，每种问题要的输出形式也不一样。
t.en: The whole machine starts as a vision test station. It computes nothing and cannot touch a single pixel: it looks at the image, reads the outputs other vision systems hand in, and judges which of them answers a request. One image can be asked many kinds of question, and each kind needs its own form of output.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：图里有哪些物体、它们在哪里，一个答案至少要带上哪些信息？每一轮有两个问题和三份输出，每份输出照原样写出它说了什么。为每个问题选出刚好够回答它的那一份：缺了信息不够，多带了不需要的也不算刚好。
t.en: This level asks: which objects are in the image and where are they — what must an answer contain at the least? Each round has two questions and three outputs, each written out exactly as it was handed in. Give every question the output that is just enough to answer it: an output missing something falls short, and one carrying more than is needed is not just enough either.
